title: Efficiency Playbook: Visual Tiles & Progressive Onboarding for Quant, Batching, and KV Cache
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a compact, progressive onboarding module ("Efficiency Playbook") that uses visual "tiles" to teach users batching, KV prefix caching, and quantization trade-offs. Deliver final Figma artboards, annotated product screenshots for the Console release, and a short microcopy library for the guide. The module should be multi-state: initial recommendation, simulated savings preview, and confirm/apply with a lightweight explainer panel.
acceptance_criteria: Figma file with 6 annotated artboards (desktop + responsive variants)
3 product screenshots (recommended state, preview with cost graph, applied state) exported at 1x and 2x
Microcopy set (40 strings) reviewed and approved by PM and Content
Design tokens and spacing spec provided to engineers in token-friendly JSON (handoff link)
Accessibility checks: color contrast >= 4.5:1 for primary text, keyboard focus states documented
tasks: Sketch initial tile concepts and onboarding flow
Write microcopy variations for tooltips and apply confirmations
Export annotated screenshots and create screenshot checklist for QA
Run design review with PM/Eng and iterate
Finalize handoff package and update Confluence doc
screenshots_required: Console - Efficiency Playbook tile (recommended preset displayed)
Console - Preview modal with estimated cost/latency savings graph
Console - Confirmation toast and applied policy visible in Model Route page
accessibility_requirements: All interactive elements reachable via keyboard (tab order validated)
Contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 for body text on primary tiles
Aria labels for toggles and status chips
Provide alt text for all exported images (short descriptive strings included in handoff)
notes: We prefer tile-first education rather than long modals to increase completion rates.
Keep quantization language approachable: use 'smaller model sizes' + 'quality indicator' instead of model-internal jargon.
Batching recommendations should include an example payload and expected latency window (e.g., 20-50ms added at tail under heavy load).
KV cache tile to surface example hit-rate improvement with a simple animated sparkline.
Screenshot guideline: include real-ish data but obfuscate customer IDs and API keys before capture.
